newsitem.title: UK: BP South Korean venture expand solvent plant.
newsitem.headline: BP South Korean venture expand solvent plant.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc on Monday said it and its venture partners Korea Alcohol Industrial and Sumitomo Corp agreed to raise production capacity of the International Esters Company (IEC) plant in South Korea.
BP added it was also looking to invest in other solvents businesses elsewhere in the Far East.
Capacity at the Korean plant will meanwhile be raised from 45,000 tonnes of ethyl acetate per year to an annual 75,000 tonnes of both ethyl and butyl acetate by early 1998, BP said.
To achieve the increase, the IEC plant at Ulsan will start making use of a new BP Chemical Solvents process technology, while BP raised its IEC stake to 45 percent from 20 percent.
"We also have plans for further solvents investments, using other new, in-house technologies, in South East Asia and China," said Didier Baudrand, leader of BP's Chemicals Solvents Business Unit.
"We are currently having discussions with potential local joint venture partners and evaluating site locations," he said in a statement.
